The work needed to bring a charge $q$ from infinity to a point is $W = qV$, where $V$ is the potential at that point.
The third corner is at a distance $r = 3\ \text{cm} = 0.03\ \text{m}$ from each of the two charges.
The potential at the third corner is $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{(q_1+q_2)}{r} = \frac{9\times10^9 \times (1+2)\times10^{-9}}{0.03}\ \text{V}$.
This gives $V = \frac{27}{0.03}\ \text{V} = 900\ \text{V}$.
So $W = qV = (3\times10^{-9}\ \text{C})(900\ \text{V}) = 2.7\times10^{-6}\ \text{J} = 2.7\ \mu\text{J}$.
Answer: (C) 2.7
